rows.grounds: gerundive expressing capability or possibility of attainment

items.question: Can the Lord be attained without the practice of devotion?
premises: The Lord is described as attainable.
Attainment is stated to be possible without devotion.
The Lord is directly addressed as the one who can be attained.
items.inference: Therefore, devotion is not presented as a necessary condition for attaining the Lord.
uncertainties: The contextual scope of 'without devotion' in relation to the preceding verses is not fully explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: O Lord, you can be attained even without devotion.
